title: GlossaryTermProperty
description: A typed property that a glossary term declares for itself and, when inheritable, for every term below it. See ADR:2026-11-12-glossary-terms-declare-their-own-properties-and-values.

glossaryTermPropertyDatatype.description: Datatype of a glossary term property. Values are stored as lexical strings and checked against the matching XSD datatype.

glossaryTermPropertyValues.description: Values of a glossary term property, as lexical strings. An empty list means the term deliberately has no value.

effectiveGlossaryTermProperty.description: A property a glossary term has, declared by the term itself or inherited from an ancestor, with the values that apply to the term.

declaredBy.description: The glossary term that declares the property.

inherited.description: True when another term declares the property.

values.description: Values that apply to this term. Empty when the property has no value here.

valuesFrom.description: The glossary term whose entry supplied the values. Absent when no entry applies.

name.description: Name of the property. Values are keyed by it, so it never changes.

displayName.description: Label shown for the property. It can change at any time.

datatype.description: Datatype of the property's values. It never changes after the property is declared.

enumValues.description: Allowed values of an `enum` property. Required for `enum` and rejected otherwise.

unit.description: Display unit for the values. Nothing converts between units.

multiValued.description: When true the property holds up to 100 values. Allowed for `string` and `enum` only.

inheritable.description: When true every term below the declaring term gets the property and can inherit its value.
